body.p: Applicant has reviewed the final Office action dated May 20, 2022, and the references cited therein. Claims 1-13 and 16 are currently pending. Claim 16 is withdrawn from consideration. Claims 1-13 stand rejected. Claims 14-15 were previously canceled. Applicant's Amendments to the Claims

In view of the final Office action's reliance upon further teachings of the previously-cited Berg reference, Applicant has amended independent claim 1 to more particularly define Applicant's claimed invention. In particular, Applicant has amended independent claim as follows:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the wearable device comprising:
a carrier configured to fit, while in use, fully around the human body, at an
abdominal part thereof; and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes,
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier
comprise one or more first electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body near the thoracic diaphragm, said first electrodes
being configured to cooperatively receive a first electrical signal indicative of a
membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the body;
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier
further comprises at least one second electrode in addition to the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to be in
contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body simultaneously
with the first electrodes that receive the first electric signal indicative of said

membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm of the body, wherein the carrier comprises a belt, and wherein the at least one second electrode and the one or more first electrodes are arranged on the belt, such that the at least one second
electrode is and to be aligned with the one or more first electrodes, the at least one
second electrode thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal indicative of one or more further electric physiologic signals from the body, for
enabling filtering of the first electrical signal using the second electrical signal for
enabling electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm.
Applicant, in accordance with the original disclosure, has amended the claims to more particularly specify that the first electrode and the second electrode are arranged on a belt and
wherein the first and second electrodes are aligned on the belt. See Applicant's original specification at page 4, lines 11-19 as well as FIGs. 2B, 2C, 3, and 6A-F.
Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the grounds for rejection of the

previously pending claims in view of Applicant's further amendments to the claims and remarks addressing the shortcomings of the prior art with regard to particular recited elements of the claimed invention.
Please charge any fee deficiencies to Deposit Account No. 12-1216. Grounds for Rejecting the Claims
1. Claims 1-5 and 11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Berg, U.S. Pub. No. 2015/0148619 (Berg).
2. Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of McGrane, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0019988 (McGrane).
3. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of Maesani, U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0273590 (Maesani).
4. Claims 8 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of Maesani as applied to claim 7, and in further view of Muccio, U.S. Pub No. 2012/0016440 (Muccio).
5. Claim 9 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg in view of Hsiao, U.S. Pub. No. 2012/0265025 (Hsiao).
6. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Sims, U.S. Pub. No. 2007/0293781 (Sims).
7. Claim 13 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Berg as applied to claim 1, and further in view of Tupin, U.S. Pub. No. 2011/0060215 (Tupin).

Applicant, in view of the current further amendments to claim 1, traverses the grounds for each and every rejection for at least the reasons set forth herein below. Applicant addresses the specific rejections in the order they arise in the Office Action.
Applicant's Specific Responses to the Grounds for Rejection
1. Rejection of Claims 1-5 and 11 as anticipated by Berg

Applicant traverses the rejection of claims 1-5 and 11, as being anticipated by the teachings of Berg. Berg does not anticipate any of the currently pending claims since the teachings of the cited Berg reference do not describe each recited element of any currently pending claim for at least the reasons stated herein below.

Moreover, a proper reason cannot be established, based upon the teachings of Berg, for one skilled in the art to modify Berg's teachings, in a way that would result in Applicant's claimed invention. Notably, none of the references demonstrates any awareness of a particularized problem that would provide a reason to modify Berg in a way that resulted in Applicants' claimed invention.
a. Applicant's Claimed Invention
Applicant's claimed invention is directed to a wearable device including a particular

electrode arrangement that facilitates monitoring vital signs (i.e., carrying out electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm) of its wearer. In particular claim 1, provided in clean form below, recites:
A wearable device for monitoring one or more vital signs of a human
body, the wearable device comprising:
a carrier configured to fit, while in use, fully around the human body, at an
abdominal part thereof; and
an electrode arrangement comprising a plurality of conductive electrodes,

wherein the electrodes are arranged on the carrier to be brought in contact with a skin of the body in use, and wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes are configured for operating simultaneously to receive electric physiologic signals from the body for enabling monitoring of a membrane potential of one or more
muscles in the body,
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier

comprise one or more first electrodes arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a side part of a torso of the body near the thoracic diaphragm, said first electrodes being configured to cooperatively receive a first electrical signal indicative of a
membrane potential of a thoracic diaphragm of the body;
wherein the plurality of conductive electrodes arranged on the carrier

further comprises at least one second electrode in addition to the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode being arranged on the carrier to be in contact with a mid front part of the abdominal part of the body simultaneously

with the first electrodes that receive the first electric signal indicative of said membrane potential of the thoracic diaphragm of the body, wherein the carrier comprises a belt, and wherein the at least one second electrode and the one or more first electrodes are arranged on the belt, such that the at least one second electrode is aligned with the one or more first electrodes, the at least one second electrode thereby being arranged for receiving a second electrical signal indicative of one or more further electric physiologic signals from the body, for enabling filtering of the first electrical signal using the second electrical signal for enabling
electromyography of the thoracic diaphragm. (Emphasis added).
Thus, Applicant's claimed invention provides a particular arrangement, including first

electrodes and second electrodes, for monitoring activity of the thoracic diaphragm. Applicant's currently clarified claimed invention defines a configuration of the first/second electrodes on a belt, and the first and second electrodes are aligned (on the belt) for particularly monitoring activity of the thoracic diaphragm of a wearer (e.g. the diaphragm of an infant}. In that regard, the claimed invention recites placing the electrodes at aligned positions on a belt to be placed on a wearer to specifically enable acquiring signals indicating the activity of the thoracic diaphragm, which are relatively weaker (and thus more difficult to sense) than a cardiac signal. See Applicant's specification at page 3, lines 13-14. Furthermore, as shown in Applicant's FIG. 2a (included below), the thoracic diaphragm (element 16) of a baby has a curved shape. Applicant's claimed second electrode provides an additional signal that is taken from the mid front part of the body. The signal provided by the second electrode includes distortions as well as the relatively/comparatively strong cardiac signal, but does not include the thoracic diaphragm signal that, due to the curved shape of the baby's diaphragm and the (claimed) aligned arrangement of the first and second electrodes along the belt, is much weaker or absent in the area where the second electrode's signal is acquired. See Applicant's specification at page 4, lines 3-19. In this regard, Applicant's FIGs. 2a, 2b and 2c are reproduced below that illustratively depict placement of the belt (and first/second electrodes) on a pre-term baby to facilitate acquiring signals via the first and second electrodes in accordance with Applicant's claimed invention.

FIG. 2a depicts the curved shape of the thoracic diaphragm 16. See Applicant's specification at page 12, lines 2-5. Applicant's FIGs. 2b and 2c illustratively depict positioning of the belt with respect to the baby's front side and back side. The location of electrode 20 on the mid front side (per FIG. 2b) is advantageous over the back side - in view of the presence of the spine which diminishes the filter signal. See Applicant's specification at page 12, lines 6-12. Applicant's claimed invention is directed to a combination of first and second electrodes, and placement of specific ones of these two distinct electrodes, at specifically recited areas of the wearer, that facilitates obtaining: (1) a raw signal containing the thoracic diaphragm signal (as well as other non-thoracic diaphragm signals), and (2) a signal that facilitates filtering non-diaphragm signals to from the raw signal to obtain the thoracic diaphragm signal.
b. The Cited Berg Reference does not anticipate Applicant's claimed invention
An annotated/edited version of Berg's FIG. 3B is provided below, wherein the added dashed lines indicate the areas to the side where (per Applicant's now-clarified claim 1) the
thoracic diaphragm signal can be sensed, and the mid front part wherein a filter signal is obtainable.
Berg indeed describes measuring thoracic activity (i.e. monitoring activity within the

thorax region of a human anatomy). However, "thoracic activity" appears (in the case of Berg's disclosure) to refer to the activity of the heart and lungs. The "thoracic diaphragm" is actually a divider between the thorax and abdomen. Nowhere does Berg even remotely suggest that the sensors provided in the shirt are capable of sensing anything other than heart and lung activity.
Berg does not describe/discuss measuring an EMG of the diaphragm of a user -

especially in the particular context of the unique anatomy of a baby. As such, Berg does not describe Applicant's further clarified "aligned" layout of first and second electrodes on a belt, and a resulting combination of signals that may be used to perform EMG of a baby's thoracic diaphragm. As previously noted, Berg merely mentions measuring thoracic activity in general.

However, given the placement of the sensors in FIG. 3B, Berg is merely generally describing acquiring EMG signals (from sensors placed at the upper torso). Berg does not describe an arrangement that is capable of acquiring an EMG signal that measures activity of the thoracic diaphragm, and certainly not an aligned arrangement of the first and second sensors on a belt that facilitates providing a filtered signal enabling monitoring of thoracic diaphragm activity of a baby.

Moreover, Berg does not describe/suggest obtaining a filter signal from a different part of the wearer's body that enables measuring a specific (relatively weak) signal of the thoracic diaphragm, by filtering out other signals using the filter signal. In particular, Berg does not describe/suggest the above-mentioned combination of electrodes/signals in the particular acquisition locations to provide a thoracic diaphragm signal from a raw sensor signal and a second (filtering) signal that facilitates rendering a filtered signal containing the thoracic diaphragm signal. In that regard, Berg is silent with regard to positioning the sensors on the torso in a way that enables, through the claimed filtering, providing an EMG signal of the thoracic diaphragm.

The thoracic diaphragm signal is very difficult to monitor accurately, because it is a weak signal among relatively strong signals (e.g., heartbeat, the lungs, muscle motion). See Applicant's Specification, at page 3, lines 13-20. To obtain a good signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) while providing a small carrier (see Specification at page 11, lines 20-25), Applicant's claimed arrangement of first and second electrodes aligned on a belt exploits the anatomic shape of the wearer's thoracic diaphragm to obtain signals: (1) near the diaphragm, and (2) remotely therefrom. See Applicant's Specification at page 4, lines 3-19. Neither the aforementioned problem, nor Applicant's specified/claimed solution are even remotely contemplated by Berg.
Applicant submits that the previous claims distinguished over the teachings of Berg.

However, the present amendments (directed to a physical configuration facilitating carrying out the intended solution) unequivocally distinguish Applicant's claimed invention over the teachings of Berg.

Thus, for the reasons set forth above, Berg does not describe an arrangement capable properly monitoring a thoracic diaphragm signal, nor does Berg describe Applicant's now- recited specific aligned configuration on a belt to facilitate obtaining a properly filtered thoracic diaphragm signal.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant's currently amended independent claim 1 is not anticipated by Berg.
